intro: Picture this: your flight lands at U-Tapao late at night, or you've got an early-morning departure, and you don't feel like the tiring drive into Pattaya — La'moon Resort is a small resort of about 24 rooms in Plutaluang, Sattahip District, Chonburi, a zone that runs into Ban Chang and sits just about 13 km from U-Tapao International Airport (UTP) · it's not a beachfront hotel in central Pattaya, but a simple small-resort-style stay that's all about location and price convenience · the rooms are air-conditioned with a fridge, TV, and kettle, plus free parking and free Wi-Fi · it's close to the Navy Plutaluang golf course, the Chee Chan golf course, and Khao Chi Chan · prices start around THB 1,200/night — there still aren't many reviews online, so this article gathers what we could actually find, along with what you should know before booking, straight up.

body.html: Who La'moon Resort is for, in a nutshell — if we sum it up as briefly as possible, La'moon Resort sells "a location near U-Tapao Airport at an affordable price" rather than luxury or sea views · it's not a beachfront high-rise, nor a big resort with an infinity pool and a grand lobby · it's a simple stay of about 24 rooms in Plutaluang, Sattahip District, Chonburi, a zone that runs into Ban Chang and sits within easy reach of U-Tapao International Airport (UTP) · its position is clearly that of a transit stay and a base for people with things to do in the Sattahip area, rather than a holiday destination in its own right · the people it suits are travelers who land at U-Tapao late or have an early departure and want a comfortable place to sleep near the airport, golfers coming to play the Navy Plutaluang or Chee Chan courses, people with official business or visiting family in the Sattahip naval district, and budget travelers using their own car who don't mind being away from central Pattaya · if you're after a beachfront stay, walking distance to Pattaya's restaurants and nightlife, or a plush room with the full facilities of a big resort, this may not be the answer, and you should consider hotels in central Pattaya, Jomtien, or Bang Saray instead · we have to be honest that online reviews of La'moon Resort are still few and scattered, so we've written this review on the basis of information we could actually verify, and we point out clearly what you should ask about before booking, so nobody ends up expecting the wrong kind of place.

Location and getting around — this is the main reason people choose to stay at La'moon Resort · it's located at Moo 5, Plutaluang Subdistrict, Sattahip District, Chonburi, a zone near Ban Chang that sits about 13 km from U-Tapao International Airport (UTP), or roughly a 15–20 min drive · for anyone with a late or early flight, that distance is a real advantage, because you don't have to drive into Pattaya (which is another 30–40 minutes away) · the area around the resort is residential and naval district land, fairly quiet and laid-back rather than a busy tourist strip · the spots nearby that guests often drop by are the Navy Plutaluang golf course and the Chee Chan golf course, both about a 10-minute drive, plus Khao Chi Chan (the Buddha image carved into the cliff face) and Ramayana Water Park, all within a short drive · quiet nearby beaches like Nang Rong Beach and the Navy's Toey Ngam Beach are also not far, good for a family swim · the honest watch-out is that Plutaluang is most convenient when you have your own car or a rental, because public transport and songthaews are far scarcer than in Pattaya, so without a car you'll rely on Grab or taxis, which can be hard to hail at times and where fares into town add up — that's worth weighing before booking, especially if you plan to head into Pattaya every day.

"Our flight landed at U-Tapao close to midnight, so we found a place near the airport in advance · the drive from the airport took under half an hour, the room was clean and comfortable enough to sleep, and in the morning we made it back to the airport in time for our flight without sweating the traffic in town. Worth what we paid."

Room types and decor — at around 24 rooms, La'moon Resort falls into the small-stay group where things get looked after fairly closely · the rooms are simple, in resort/guesthouse style, air-conditioned throughout, with the basic essentials covered: a fridge, a flat-screen TV with cable channels, an electric kettle, a desk, and a private bathroom with a hot shower, plus bathroom amenities and slippers, drinking water, and free Wi-Fi · from the information available, there are both standard rooms and family rooms, and some rooms are pet-friendly for an extra charge that you need to ask about in advance · the decor isn't fancy, leaning toward clean and practical over design · in terms of setting expectations, think of this as "a clean bedroom for a pre/post-flight stay," not a plush resort room you'd lounge in all day · because there still aren't many reviews online, the details worth confirming clearly at the time of booking are the actual room size, the number of beds, the room's current condition, and whether the hot water/air-con work well · with a small stay like this, room condition can vary from unit to unit, so flagging your needs (for example, asking for a freshly cleaned room, or a ground-floor room if you have heavy luggage) when you book will help the stay go smoothly.

Facilities and common areas — La'moon Resort is a small stay with facilities that are "enough for a transit stay" rather than a resort you come to for the facilities themselves · what's confirmed from the information is free parking (a big deal for anyone driving their own car or a rental), free Wi-Fi in the common areas, reception, luggage storage, a garden, and an on-site restaurant/cafe · some booking platforms list a swimming pool and spa service, but to be straight with you, that part isn't consistently clear across every channel · so if a pool or spa is something that matters to your decision, you should call or message the property directly before booking to confirm whether it's actually open during the period you're going — don't go off the platform photos alone · the genuine advantage here is being a small, quiet stay with easy parking, which makes an overnight near the airport more convenient · in short, if you're coming to "sleep easy, park easily, get out to the airport fast," the facilities on offer are enough, but if you expect to spend the whole day with a pool and spa at the property, check first to be sure.

Food and eats around the property — there's an on-site restaurant/cafe, handy for an easy meal or a morning coffee before you head off · but the area's real food strength lies in the restaurants and markets across the Sattahip–Plutaluang area, known for fresh, fairly priced seafood, since this is a navy seaside town · guests who drive themselves tend to head out for food in Sattahip town or around Ban Chang, which have a decent spread of restaurants, convenience stores, and coffee shops · worth knowing: the area right around the property doesn't have a dense cluster of late-night spots like Pattaya does, so if you arrive late, bring some food with you or plan to stop and pick something up on the way from the airport · breakfast depends on the package you book — some rates may not include it, so check the conditions clearly when you book · overall, food at La'moon Resort isn't the reason to come and eat at the property itself; it's a helpful add-on, while the real good eats are in the surrounding Sattahip area, waiting for you to go and try.

Service — for a small stay like this, service tends to be friendly and hands-on, run by a small team of a few people · there's reception and basic services like luggage storage and help coordinating travel · what guests at small stays like this often get is the closeness and flexibility — for instance, talking over check-in/check-out times that can flex a bit to match your flight (subject to room availability and agreeing in advance) · because La'moon Resort positions itself as a transit stay near the airport, asking ahead about airport pickup/drop-off or advice on transport is something worth doing before you travel · the thing to understand is that with its small size and format, some things a big hotel has — like 24-hour room service or a full tour desk — may not all be there · and since there are still few reviews, there isn't a solid enough overall picture of the service to call it definitively, so communicating directly with the property before your stay is the best way to set the right expectations.

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — we have to be honest that La'moon Resort is a small stay where online reviews are still few and scattered across Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and other booking platforms; some have only a handful of reviews or almost none, so we can't sum up a reliable overall score the way you can for popular hotels · from what we could gather, the praise tends to circle around things that match the property's selling point: the location near U-Tapao Airport that's handy for a pre/post-flight stay, the free parking and easy in-and-out by car, the quiet of the area, and the affordable price · the watch-outs to brace for are that it's a small stay with fewer facilities than a big resort, that it's away from central Pattaya and you have to rely on your own car, that the consistency of room condition and service may depend on the time given the small team, and that details like the pool/spa/breakfast are best confirmed before booking · because the review data is thin, we suggest looking at this place with the expectation of "a budget transit stay near the airport" and checking all the conditions before you hit book, rather than expecting a full-on holiday resort experience.

"The good part is it's near U-Tapao Airport and has parking, and the price isn't expensive · but you have to understand it's a small place, nothing fancy, and fairly far from Pattaya, so it's a bit of a hassle without a car. Next time, if we're staying before a flight, we'd pick here again."

Price comparison and value — La'moon Resort's starting price is around THB 1,200/night in normal pricing (you'll sometimes find lower rates for a standard room), and it may climb during long weekends or festivals · viewed as "a budget stay near U-Tapao Airport," this price is accessible and good value for an overnight before or after a flight, especially once you count the free parking and the ease of driving in and out of the airport · compared with staying at a hotel in Pattaya and driving to and from the airport each time, staying near U-Tapao saves both time and the fatigue of travel days · but compared as "a base for a Pattaya holiday," this price may not be as good value as a stay in Jomtien or Bang Saray that's closer to the beach and restaurants, because you'll rack up extra travel costs into town · in short, La'moon Resort's value depends directly on the purpose of your trip: great value if you're coming for transit or have business in Sattahip, but maybe not the best-value option if your main goal is sightseeing in Pattaya.

What to know before booking — a few things help the stay go smoothly · one, confirm the actual location and distance to U-Tapao Airport with the property if you have a late/early flight, so you can plan your travel time just right · two, the Plutaluang area is most convenient with your own car or a rental; if you don't have a car, ask about airport pickup/drop-off or have the Grab app ready, and allow extra time · three, some facilities — like a swimming pool, spa, and breakfast — should be confirmed directly with the property as actually open during your dates, because the information across platforms doesn't always match · four, if you're bringing a pet, ask about the conditions and extra charges in advance · five, because it's a small stay with few reviews, we suggest choosing free cancellation first if your plans aren't firm, and comparing prices/conditions across several platforms (Agoda, Booking, Trip.com) before deciding · six, if you're arriving late, let the property know your approximate check-in time in advance to make sure someone is there to check you in.

Bottom line — from the information and reviews we could actually find, La'moon Resort is the stay that suits best for anyone who needs a budget place near U-Tapao Airport for a pre/post-flight stay, or who has business in the Sattahip–Plutaluang area · its strengths are a location just about 13 km from U-Tapao Airport (UTP), free parking, the quiet of the area, and an accessible price · if you land at U-Tapao late, have an early departure, are a golfer coming to play the Navy or Chee Chan courses, or travel by your own car, this is a sensible overnight on a comfortable budget · but if you're looking for a beachfront stay, walking distance to restaurants and nightlife, or the full facilities of a big resort and plenty of reviews to feel sure, this may not be the answer, and you should consider hotels in central Pattaya, Jomtien, or Bang Saray instead · most importantly, since online reviews are still few, ask the property directly about the key details and pick a flexible cancellation option first — and then a stay at La'moon Resort will be a good-value, convenient transit choice for a trip that starts or ends at U-Tapao.

faq.q: Where is La'moon Resort, and how far is it from U-Tapao Airport?
faq.a: The property is at Moo 5, Plutaluang Subdistrict, Sattahip District, Chonburi, in the zone near Ban Chang · it's about 13 km, or roughly a 15–20 min drive, from U-Tapao International Airport (UTP) · it's close to the Navy Plutaluang golf course, the Chee Chan golf course, and Khao Chi Chan · central Pattaya is about a 30–40 min drive away.

It's a great fit for anyone who needs a budget stay near U-Tapao Airport for a pre/post-flight stop, golfers coming to play in the Sattahip area, and people with business in the Plutaluang district · it has free parking and sits in a quiet area · if your main goal is a beachfront stay or nightlife in Pattaya, a hotel in central Pattaya, Jomtien, or Bang Saray may suit you better.

faq.q: What's the starting price at La'moon Resort, and what room types are there?

faq.a: Some booking platforms list a swimming pool and spa service, but that information isn't consistently clear across every channel, and breakfast depends on the package you book · we suggest confirming directly with the property before booking that it's actually open during the period you're going — don't go off the platform photos alone · the property has an on-site restaurant/cafe, a garden, and free Wi-Fi.

faq.q: Do you need your own car to get to La'moon Resort?
faq.a: You don't have to have one, but having your own car or a rental is most convenient, because public transport in Plutaluang is far scarcer than in Pattaya · the property has free parking · if you don't have a car, ask about airport pickup/drop-off, have the Grab app ready, and allow extra time/fare when you need to head into town.
